questions.prompt: The enemy had destroyed the walls before the consul arrived.
questions.answer: Hostēs mūrōs, antequam cōnsul advēnit, dēlērant.

questions.prompt: You have loved the fatherland more than your own life.
questions.answer: Patriam plūs quam vītam tuam amāstī.

questions.prompt: The soldiers filled the ditch with earth and rushed forward.
questions.answer: Mīlitēs fossam terrā complērunt et prōcurrērunt.

questions.prompt: Would that you had freed the captives who begged for mercy!
questions.answer: Utinam captīvōs, quī veniam ōrāvērunt, līberāssētis!

questions.prompt: You have known that man's character for many years.
questions.answer: Illīus virī mōrēs multōs annōs nōstī.

questions.prompt: The senators had removed the impatient tribune from the assembly.
questions.answer: Senātōrēs impatientem tribūnum ex cōntiōne remōrant.

questions.prompt: Have you heard the rumor that spread through the whole city?
questions.answer: Rūmōrem quī per tōtam urbem mānāvit audīstis?

questions.prompt: I would not have known such grief unless you had departed.
questions.answer: Tantum dolōrem nōn nōssem nisi discessissēs.

questions.prompt: The war must be waged with great courage.
questions.answer: Bellum magnā virtūte gerundum est.

questions.prompt: By seizing the citadel the general ended the war.
questions.answer: Arce capiundā dux bellum cōnfēcit.

questions.prompt: There was no hope of taking the city by force.
questions.answer: Nūlla spēs erat urbis vī capiundae.

questions.prompt: These things must be said openly before the people.
questions.answer: Haec apertē apud populum dīcunda sunt.

questions.prompt: Lead the troops across the mountains at once, general.
questions.answer: Dūc cōpiās trāns montēs statim, dux.

questions.prompt: Tell me the truth about that dubious matter.
questions.answer: Dīc mihi vērum dē illā dubiā rē.

questions.prompt: Do what the law commands, and fear nothing.
questions.answer: Fac quod lēx iubet, et nihil timē.

questions.prompt: Finish the work quickly, soldier, before night falls.
questions.answer: Opus celeriter cōnfice, mīles, antequam nox cadit.

questions.prompt: It is right that virtue be praised by all.
questions.answer: Fās est virtūtem ab omnibus laudārier.

questions.prompt: They forbade the gates to be opened at night.
questions.answer: Portās nocte aperīrier vetuērunt.

questions.prompt: The general ordered the camp to be fortified quickly.
questions.answer: Dux castra celeriter mūnīrier iussit.

questions.prompt: It was not permitted for the truth to be spoken.
questions.answer: Vērum dīcier nōn licēbat.

questions.prompt: I used to hear the birds singing at dawn in the woods.
questions.answer: Avēs in silvīs prīmā lūce canentēs audībam.

questions.prompt: I shall know the whole truth when the messenger returns.
questions.answer: Tōtum vērum scībō ubi nūntius redierit.

questions.prompt: The soldiers used to guard the walls throughout the night.
questions.answer: Mīlitēs mūrōs tōtā nocte custōdībant.

questions.prompt: I did not know then how great the danger was.
questions.answer: Tum quantum perīculum esset nescībam.

questions.prompt: You had loved the queen long before her exile.
questions.answer: Rēgīnam multō ante exsilium eius amārās.

questions.prompt: The citizens had destroyed the temple that the king had built.
questions.answer: Cīvēs templum quod rēx aedificāverat dēlērant.

questions.prompt: The soldiers heard the trumpet in the silent night.
questions.answer: Mīlitēs tubam nocte silentī audīrunt.

questions.prompt: Would that you had known the danger before you had set out!
questions.answer: Utinam perīculum nōssēs antequam profectus essēs!

questions.prompt: The bridge must be built before the enemy arrive.
questions.answer: Pōns faciundus est priusquam hostēs adveniant.

questions.prompt: For the sake of defending the walls the soldiers kept watch.
questions.answer: Moenium dēfendundōrum causā mīlitēs vigilābant.

questions.prompt: Great was the desire of seizing power among the nobles.
questions.answer: Magna erat capiundī imperiī cupīdō inter nōbilēs.

questions.prompt: The fields must be tilled before winter comes.
questions.answer: Agrī ante hiemem colundī sunt.

questions.prompt: Lead your men out of the valley, brave general.
questions.answer: Ēdūc tuōs ē valle, fortis dux.

questions.prompt: Finish the work, then tell me the truth.
questions.answer: Cōnfice opus, deinde dīc mihi vērum.

questions.prompt: Make a fire, friend, and lead the horses to the river.
questions.answer: Fac ignem, amīce, et dūc equōs ad flūmen.

questions.prompt: Speak the truth boldly, and do what your duty demands.
questions.answer: Dīc audācter vērum, et fac quod officium poscit.

questions.prompt: The shepherds used to hear the pipe among the hills.
questions.answer: Pāstōrēs tībiam inter collēs audībant.

questions.prompt: Soon I shall know whither fortune is leading us.
questions.answer: Mox scībō quō fortūna nōs dūcat.

questions.prompt: The captives kept begging to be freed at last.
questions.answer: Captīvī tandem līberārier ōrābant.

questions.prompt: You have said many things about the war, but done few.
questions.answer: Multa dē bellō dīxtī, sed pauca fēcistī.

questions.prompt: He promised that he would come at first light.
questions.answer: Prīmā lūce ventūrum sē pollicitus est.

questions.prompt: Yesterday the scouts reported that the bridge had been broken by the river.
questions.answer: Herī explōrātōrēs pontem flūmine ruptum nūntiāvērunt.

questions.prompt: Would that the gods might grant us peace at last!
questions.answer: Utinam dī nōbīs tandem pācem duint!

questions.prompt: The seer foretold that a great war would soon arise.
questions.answer: Vātēs magnum bellum mox ortūrum praedīxit.

questions.prompt: Tears with their moisture ate away her bloodless cheeks.
questions.answer: Lacrimae perēdēre hūmōre exsanguēs genās.

questions.prompt: At the servant's instruction they set before her only one vessel of vinegar, whose sharpness and power dissolves pearls into a liquid.
questions.answer: Ex praeceptō ministrī ūnum tantum vās ante eam posuēre acētī, cuius asperitās vīsque in tābem margarītās resolvit.

questions.prompt: Lead out with you also all your followers; if not, then as many as possible — purge the city!
questions.answer: Ēdūc tēcum etiam omnēs tuōs: sī minus, quam plūrimōs — pūrgā urbem!
